wave: CENSUS BLINDNESS -- code_analyze's own census.coverage.BUILD never promoted, contradicting its own reported dependency_closure
wave_title: runtime::code_analyze computes a real dependency_closure and reports it as a top-level JSON field, but never fed its state back into census.coverage.BUILD the way runtime::systemize does -- so a single atlas-cli code analyze response could simultaneously report dependency_closure.state: CLOSED and census.coverage.BUILD: UNSUPPORTED for the exact same repository, a direct self-contradiction within one report.

generation_model.G_n: 0a90ffe2f9 (fix(declared): correct WebUI materialization path to apps/studio) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct re-census of this repository's own real state via `atlas-cli code analyze --root .` (not delegated to an agent), inspecting the raw JSON output for anomalies rather than assuming prior fixes covered every entry point. Found `census.coverage.BUILD: UNSUPPORTED` in the same response that reported `dependency_closure.state: CLOSED` with 29 real edges -- immediately recognized as the same 'BUILD never promoted' defect class `runtime::systemize` already had fixed for itself (this session's earlier `resolve_dependency_closure`/`build_coverage_from_dependency_closure` wiring), just not propagated to this second, separate entry point built on the same underlying data.

priority_classification: census blindness (priority 4) -- one of Atlas's own canonical report-producing entry points contradicted itself about a directly checkable fact (whether the Cargo dependency closure had been observed), which is exactly the class of self-inconsistency this session has repeatedly found and fixed across other entry points (the `coding_admission`/`check` disagreement fixed several generations ago is the same shape of bug: one code path correctly derives a fact, a sibling code path building on the same underlying data does not).

design_decisions.question: Duplicate systemize's promotion logic inline in code_analyze, or refactor further?
design_decisions.decision: Reuse the exact same already-tested pure function (`build_coverage_from_dependency_closure`) `systemize` already uses, applied to `code_analyze`'s own already-computed `dependency_closure` (which the graph-projection work earlier this session added to `code_analyze` for an unrelated reason -- projecting it into the graph). No new logic was written; this is purely a wiring fix reusing existing, already-falsified logic (5 existing tests in runtime/src/lib.rs cover every `DependencyClosureState` transition for this exact function), so no new test was added -- the fix's correctness rests entirely on that already-established test coverage plus direct real-repository verification.

design_decisions.question: Should code_analyze also gain a coding_admission/blockers field to match systemize?
design_decisions.decision: No -- out of scope for this fix. `code_analyze`'s own schema/purpose (`atlas.systemizer.code-analysis.v3`, 'derived engineering analysis; target repositories remain sovereign') is a raw diagnostic dump, not a gated readiness report; it has never had a `coding_admission` field and adding one would be an unrelated scope expansion. This fix only makes the `census.coverage.BUILD` field it already reports accurate, not add a new gating concept to an endpoint that was never meant to gate anything.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: `atlas-cli code analyze`'s `census.coverage.BUILD` value now agrees with its own `dependency_closure.state` in the same response, using the identical, already-verified promotion rule `systemize` uses (`Closed` -> `Observed`, `Partial`/`Blocked` -> `Unknown`, `NotApplicable` -> unchanged).
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: No new test needed: the promotion function itself (`build_coverage_from_dependency_closure`) already has 5 falsification tests covering every state transition, written when `systemize`'s own version of this bug was fixed earlier this session. This change is pure wiring reuse of that already-proven logic in a second call site.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Ran `atlas-cli code analyze --root .` against this repository's own real workspace (not a synthetic fixture): `census.coverage.BUILD` flips from `UNSUPPORTED` to `OBSERVED`, now agreeing with the same response's `dependency_closure.state: CLOSED`. Re-ran `atlas-cli systemize --root .` and `atlas-cli docs audit --root .atlas` to confirm zero regression to the unrelated, already-correct systemize path: `coding_admission.allowed` remains `true` with zero blockers (the milestone reached in the immediately prior generation).

implementation.runtime_wiring: runtime/src/lib.rs::code_analyze -- census is now `mut`; dependency_closure is computed before normalization (reordered, matching systemize's own ordering) and its build_coverage_from_dependency_closure result is applied to census.coverage.BUILD before the response is assembled

Fixed by reusing systemize's own already-tested promotion logic. Verified directly against this repository's own real state with zero regression to the unrelated, already-green systemize path.
